rationale: Submits the probe the verify account's remaining limitation called for, which shows the stale-read consequence end to end instead of arguing it from the endpoint. Each trial commits a value through the leader, waits for it to reach every node, partitions the leader from both other voters and from the non-voter, registers a VerifyLeader request, stalls the leader's main loop so its lease case cannot run, lets a voter majority elect a successor and commit a different value, then reconnects the non-voter so the acknowledgement is counted during the stall, and finally reads the stalled leader's own FSM after the verify returns. The comparison asks whether success coexisted with FSM content that differs from the successor's, using the values themselves as the witness rather than any inference from the endpoint. Execution is requested; no outcome is claimed in advance.

scope.description: Five trials that each commit a value, partition and stall the leader, let a successor commit a different value, then compare the FSM values of the stalled leader and the successor after the leader's VerifyLeader returned, recording the verify endpoint, the two values, both terms and the stall counters.
assumptions: The mock FSM records each applied command in order, so its last value is what the node's state machine holds for that key; the harness reads it through the package's own test helper rather than by reaching into raft state.
The value committed before the partition has reached every node, checked by waiting after the apply, so the two nodes start from the same state.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms, a 900ms store stall that blocks the leader's main loop, and in-memory transports in one process.
excluded: A networked deployment, and any read path other than the FSM value the mock records.

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds four real Raft instances of the same shape as the earlier witness probe: three voters bootstrapped as Voter and one non-voter joined through the leader's AddNonvoter call, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, and only the elected leader's log store armed with a 900ms stall. It emits assurance_stale_read_setup, commits the value 'old' through the leader and waits for it to appear on all nodes, disconnects the leader from both other voters and from the non-voter, registers VerifyLeader, waits 30ms, arms the stall, drives one Apply to block the leader's main loop, waits up to two seconds for another voter to report Leader and has that successor apply the value 'new', reconnects only the non-voter after the configured delay, waits for the verify future, then emits assurance_stale_read_result with the endpoint, the stalled leader's last FSM value, the successor's last FSM value, whether those differ, both terms, the stalled leader's state and the stall counters. The harness is TestAssuranceVerifyRegisteredThenStalled.

comparisons.description: Conditional on the verify reporting success: whether the stalled leader's FSM value differed from the successor's, which is the stale read a caller would have taken.
The stalled leader's own FSM never advanced past the value committed before the partition.
The successor committed the different value, so the cluster did move on while the old leader was stalled.

experiment.revision_reason: The earlier revision showed the overlap between a successful VerifyLeader and a concurrent successor but never read the stalled leader's FSM, which the account recorded as a limitation. This revision keeps the same build, partition, stall and reconnection and adds committed values: a value applied and replicated before the partition, a different value applied by the successor afterwards, and reads of the mock FSM on both nodes after the verify returns. Event names are new because the fields differ; the setup and result structure is unchanged.
